svg.title: base_state: records, links and how they are loaded
svg.desc: Animated: the DiscreteGarageState message of the running example, record by record, in the order DiscreteGarageState::Set adds them, and the checks ValidateBaseState runs afterwards.
svg.metadata: ["The garage at now, in the scenario of the time-line figure. The message lists every asset in flat arrays; links between records are ids, not pointers.", "Set() starts empty and replays one existence event per record. AGVs come first, with tray_id forced to 0, because their trays do not exist yet.", "Bays, then VECS and VRCs (none in this layout). A bay record is a state machine value and an operator flag; its position comes from the layout, since a bay's id is its node id.", "Trays. A tray with agv_id != 0 is attached to that AGV (which must be lifted, on the same node and parallel), and the AGV's tray_id is set from it: tray.agv_id is the field that counts.", "Payloads. payload.tray_id puts the car on its tray (which must be empty): tray.payload_id is filled from it. reciprocal_to_tray says the car faces the other way on the tray.", "disabled_nodes become NodeDisablednessChanged events (none here). The message's hash is not compared. Any failed event rejects the whole request: PlanResponse.success = false.", "ValidateBaseState then checks the state against the layout: every payload fits some resource window, and every AGV and tray pose exists. Only after that does the reservation loop run."]

g.text: Map labels: P17, W22, B21, C14 = node_id 17, 22, 21, 14 (P parking, W waypoint, B bay, C AGV charger); T17 = tray_id 17; AGV-1 = agv_id 1; X@90 = GaragePose {node_id: X, heading: 90}, heading in degrees [-179, 180], 90 = facing -x.
